# Contract benchmark results

<!-- Generated by scripts/run_contract_bench.py; do not edit by hand. -->

Each of the 71 specimen defects in a category Mumei targets has a requirement and one contract (requires/ensures) that the buggy and the fixed function are both checked against. The right answer is: buggy version refuted, fixed version proven. Values are medians over runs, with the range in brackets. Arm tables score the fidelity-acceptance projection; committed result JSON keeps raw verifier outcomes separately.

Outcome taxonomy: false acceptance is a buggy body proven; false positive is a fixed body refuted; unsupported means the input, generated port/contract or verifier capability cannot represent the case; inconclusive means no evidence either way; environment failure means tool/transport failure; budget exhausted means the declared timeout was consumed. These categories are mutually exclusive per-variant outcomes, not proof grades; one shared LLM request failure can therefore produce two environment-failure outcomes.

Fidelity acceptance gate: mumei + LLM (LLM ports, mumei checks) blocks 12 (12–13) candidate variant(s) per run. The committed rows keep the raw verifier proof outcome; only the report projection counts a blocked candidate as unsupported/inconclusive evidence rather than verification acceptance. Lint is variant-aware and records high-confidence meaning-loss evidence: silent repair, missing modeled operations, guard folding, self-calls and success-flag rewrites. A separate solver-backed output comparison inlines the reference and candidate bodies and compares primitive results or struct output fields. Committed per-case policy adjudicates don't-care fields, meaningful failure state and integer-rounding boundaries; matched exact output is confirming evidence, adjudicated divergence blocks, and boundary-only differences are inconclusive diagnostic evidence. Loop-containing bodies are unavailable rather than risk invariant-abstraction false positives. Confirming replay or matched output overrides guard-shape and success-flag lint-only warnings; exact result-state guard folding remains blocking unless output equality matches. Added or removed guard-count warnings stay visible without blocking alone. Replay divergence always blocks; other high-confidence lint blocks when neither replay nor output comparison supplies confirming evidence, except silent repair, missing modeled operations and self-calls, which are structural fidelity loss even when outputs coincide. Inconclusive evidence alone does not rewrite a raw proof. These are fidelity acceptance diagnostics, not formal proof verdicts. Weak/vacuous generated contracts cannot support proof acceptance. For mumei + LLM (LLM ports, mumei checks), raw verifier proofs before projection were buggy 8 (8–10) and fixed 71 (70–71) per run, while projected acceptance leaves fixed proven at 67 (66–68) and unresolved/unsupported at 13 (12–14).

Verification time and budget are wall seconds and the declared per-attempt timeout aggregated over recorded outcome-determining verifier calls, including vacuity controls, fidelity replay calls, output-equivalence calls and the per-call input/output glue inside `verify_text`. Certificate emission/rechecks, case-level orchestration and provider calls are outside that measurement. Older committed rows show the measured fraction of expected verifier calls, so partial `--only` refreshes cannot look fully instrumented. Model time/cost come only from provider usage metadata.

[REPLAY.md](REPLAY.md) replays concrete inputs, the LLM witnesses and the LLM ports on the native code (`scripts/run_native_replay.py`). [REGRESSION.md](REGRESSION.md) reads the same results as a pull-request gate for changes under a pinned contract (`scripts/run_regression_gate.py`).

The reference ports were written by hand with knowledge of the defects, so the first row shows that the contracts can express each requirement and how often the checker tells the two versions apart. It is not a detection result. The LLM rows are the comparison. LLM only and mumei + LLM see the product source file, the requirement, the modelling notes and the contract header, never the defect list or the reference ports. LLM only answers holds/violated itself; a "holds" is the model's opinion, not a proof. mumei + LLM asks the model only for the `.mm` body under the pinned header, and mumei decides.

mumei + LLM contract removes the hand-written contract instead: the model gets the requirement, the modelling notes, the prelude and the atom signature, but no code and not the reference requires/ensures. Its one contract is put on both reference bodies, so a wrong answer here is a contract-writing error: a buggy body accepted means the contract is too weak to catch the defect, a fixed body rejected means it asks for more than the requirement does. The same vacuity control as for the reference applies.

A buggy function whose LLM port mumei proves is a translation problem: the reference port of the same function under the same contract is refuted, so the LLM port does not keep the defect. mumei's verdict is only as faithful as the port it checks.

A proof covers the model in the port, not native behaviour the model leaves out, such as fixed-width overflow, nil pointers or exceptions from library calls. Some LLM-only rejections of a fixed function point at exactly that kind of behaviour; their witnesses are listed below.

Vacuity control (fixed port re-checked with `ensures: false`, must fail): 71 / 71 pass.

Proof certificates: 71 / 71 proven fixed ports have one, emitted with `mumei verify --proof-cert` and re-checked with `mumei verify-cert --strict`. Trust: Z3 71. `--check` compares each committed `fixed.proof.json` with its recorded hash and with the current `fixed.mm`.

Lean bridge dual check (mumei-lean `5005d36`): records one outcome per certified obligation. `partial_translation` means the bridge could not state the whole obligation in Lean, so nothing was checked; `stale`, `unsupported`, `timeout`, `no-certificate` and `not-checked` mean no current Lean check completed; a failed dual check does not change the Z3 result. lean_verified 22, partial_translation 49 of 71 recorded obligations (71 bridge outcomes returned).

Vacuity control for mumei + LLM contract (LLM writes the contract, reference ports) (openai/gpt-6-luna), per run: 68 / 71, 68 / 71, 67 / 71 pass. A raw verifier proof under a weak or vacuous contract still indicates a contract-writing error, but the fidelity gate keeps it out of benchmark acceptance as unsupported/inconclusive evidence.

Proof certificates for mumei + LLM (LLM ports, mumei checks) (openai/gpt-6-luna), per run: 71 / 71, 71 / 71, 70 / 70 proven fixed ports have one, emitted and re-checked like the reference ones and committed as `mumei-llm/<model>-run<n>.fixed.proof.json` next to the case. Trust: Z3 212.
